Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

negative adjective

unfavourable, bad

also a negative, negative side, downside, drawback, negative effect, unfavourable

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.102: plūs habeat adjūmentī quam incommodī (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.C. 1.48.1: accidit repentīnum incommodum

incommodus, incommoda, incommodum

adjective; as a noun, incommodum, incommodī n., a drawback, a disadvantage, declension

unfavourable, inconvenient, troublesome

The noun incommodum is the negative side of a thing, set against commodum (see advantage).

Other words

  • adversus, adversa, adversum — adverse, unfavourable (of events, winds, fortune)

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.C. 2.31.3: rēs adversae (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.C. 3.107: adversissimī nāvigantibus ventī

    Literally “turned towards, facing”; rēs adversae is misfortune, opposed to rēs secundae.

  • negātīvus, negātīva, negātīvum — that denies, negative (in logic and grammar)

    adjective, declension · avoid · post-classical · Gai. Inst. 4.3; Dig. 50.16.237 (Lewis & Short)

    A lawyers’ and grammarians’ word for a denying statement or particle, post-classical for negāns; it never meant unfavourable. For a negative answer, use negāre (see say).

Examples

  • quī locus est tālis, ut plūs habeat adjūmentī quam incommodī

    this is a point of such a kind that it brings more help than harmCic. de Or. 2.102 (Lewis & Short)

  • Habet in adversīs auxilia, quī in secundīs commodat.

    Whoever lends in good times has help in bad times.Publ. H 6

See also advantage, bad, say.
